story.soThat: Annie can trace LLM calls, tool executions, and performance metrics
story.tasks: - Task 1: Add Langfuse dependency (AC: #1) - Task 2: Create observability module structure (AC: #1, #2, #4) - Task 3: Implement Langfuse singleton client (AC: #1, #2, #5, #6) - Task 4: Implement tracing utilities (AC: #4) - Task 5: Add Langfuse configuration functions (AC: #7) - Task 6: Update environment configuration (AC: #1, #2) - Task 7: Add health check integration (AC: #3) - Task 8: Testing (AC: #1, #2, #5)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC #1: Langfuse client initializes successfully with singleton pattern and background flushing (batch_size=10, flush_interval=1s) when keys are configured AC #2: Application continues without crashes and logs "Langfuse tracing disabled" when keys are NOT configured (graceful degradation) AC #3: Health check endpoint `/health` includes Langfuse status (enabled/disabled, client availability, last flush timestamp) AC #4: Trace context maintained correctly using `contextvars` without cross-request contamination in async operations AC #5: Application continues without errors when Langfuse Cloud unavailable, logs failures at WARNING level (fire-and-forget) AC #6: `ping_langfuse()` health check returns correct status without blocking operations AC #7: Config functions return correct values with `@lru_cache`: `get_langfuse_public_key()`, `get_langfuse_secret_key()`, `get_langfuse_host()`, `is_langfuse_enabled()`

story-context.constraints: - Fire-and-Forget Pattern: Tracing failures MUST NOT impact application performance or user experience - Performance Overhead: < 10ms p95 latency overhead for tracing operations - Async-Safe Context: Use contextvars (not threading.local) for request-scoped trace context - Graceful Degradation: Application MUST continue functioning when Langfuse is unavailable or misconfigured - Singleton Lifecycle: One Langfuse client instance per backend service instance with proper atexit cleanup - No Blocking Operations: ping_langfuse() and all tracing operations must be non-blocking - Configuration Pattern: Follow existing config.py patterns with @lru_cache optimization - Sensitive Data: Add LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY to SENSITIVE_VARS list for log masking

tests.standards: Annie uses pytest and pytest-asyncio for testing. Tests are organized into unit tests (backend/tests/unit/) and integration tests (backend/tests/integration/). Unit tests use AsyncMock for external dependencies. Integration tests validate end-to-end workflows. Follow existing test patterns from test_profile_manager.py and test_llm_client.py.
tests.locations: - backend/tests/unit/ (unit tests for langfuse_client.py, tracing.py, config additions) - backend/tests/integration/ (integration test for end-to-end tracing workflow)
tests.ideas: - AC #1: Test Langfuse client initializes with valid keys (unit test with mocked Langfuse SDK) - AC #2: Test graceful degradation when keys missing (unit test verifying no crashes, correct logging) - AC #3: Test health endpoint includes Langfuse status (integration test hitting /health/detailed) - AC #4: Test contextvars isolation across concurrent async requests (unit test with asyncio.gather) - AC #5: Test fire-and-forget when Langfuse unavailable (unit test with mocked network failure) - AC #6: Test ping_langfuse() returns correct status (unit test with mocked connection states) - AC #7: Test config functions with @lru_cache (unit test verifying caching behavior and correct values) - Integration: Test complete tracing workflow from start_trace to end_span (integration test) - Edge case: Test invalid keys handled gracefully without blocking app startup - Edge case: Test atexit handler flushes traces on shutdown
